@graph.name: Entry 75: prominence-τ map treatment — the deadband's amplitude selectivity as raster preprocessing
@graph.text: No — refuted on both grids. At the primary cell (eps_geo, n = 16) the prominence-6 chain reads 7.43 med|d%| on the IGC 30 m lattice and 22.80 on FABDEM against the Gaussian's 4.23 / 4.96, with the paired test decisively against (41/150 and 16/140). The c pins carry the mechanism: prominence removes phantom ascent at 5.91 to 3.63 m/km (IGC) and barely 5.73 to 5.20 (FABDEM) vs the Gaussian's 2.53 / 2.99 — DEM noise is predominantly CONNECTED 2-D micro-structure with through-paths everywhere, not the closed pits and summits a prominence filter can see, while a 1-D transect crosses it at full amplitude. The deadband's amplitude filtering has no faithful raster analog via h-extrema; sigma-30 keeps the crown and the deployable default stands. Side-finding: a 30 m lattice point-sampled from the 5 m survey is itself a noisier chain than along-track sampling (c 5.91 vs 3.75 m/km) — regular-lattice aliasing is a grid-design cost.
